sources.title: Perspective: OLED Displays Singing with the Blues
sources.abstract: While blue pixels consume approximately 50% of the energy of organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display front planes, in the 25 years since their invention, 100% internal efficiency phosphorescent OLEDs (PHOLEDs) have not met the stability standards necessary for their adoption. In this perspective, we discuss the significant progress and challenges encountered during this long journey of exploration and discovery. Today, using a combination of solutions including robust molecular design, graded doping of the emission layer, increasing the optical density of states to decrease the triplet radiative lifetime, and employing light outcoupling schemes, deep blue PHOLEDs are now achieving lifetimes approaching those of their green analogs. This perspective elaborates on the challenges and opportunities confronting further development of triplet-controlled emitters, including PHOLEDs using heavy-metal phosphors and thermally activated delayed fluorescent OLEDs. We also address some persistent problems commonly found in the literature concerning the measurement of quantum efficiency and operational lifetime.

sources.title: Physics-Constrained Graph Neural Networks for Spatio-Temporal Prediction of Drop Impact on OLED Display Panels
sources.abstract: This study aims to predict the spatio-temporal evolution of physical quantities observed in multi-layered display panels subjected to the drop impact of a ball. To model these complex interactions, graph neural networks have emerged as promising tools, effectively representing objects and their relationships as graph structures. In particular, MeshGraphNets (MGNs) excel in capturing dynamics in dynamic physics simulations using irregular mesh data. However, conventional MGNs often suffer from non-physical artifacts, such as the penetration of overlapping objects. To resolve this, we propose a physics-constrained MGN that mitigates these penetration issues while maintaining high level of accuracy in temporal predictions. Furthermore, to enhance the model's robustness, we explore noise injection strategies with varying magnitudes and different combinations of targeted components, such as the ball, the plate, or both. In addition, our analysis on model stability in spatio-temporal predictions reveals that during the inference, deriving next time-step node positions by predicting relative changes (e.g., displacement or velocity) between the current and future states yields superior accuracy compared to direct absolute position predictions. This approach consistently shows greater stability and reliability in determining subsequent node positions across various scenarios. Building on this validated model, we evaluate its generalization performance by examining its ability to extrapolate with respect to design variables. Furthermore, the physics-constrained MGN serves as a near real-time emulator for the design optimization of multi-layered OLED display panels, where thickness variables are optimized to minimize stress in the light-emitting materials. It outperforms conventional MGN in optimization tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness for practical design applications.

sources.title: The Steady Evolution of OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract OLED's flexibility has made it the dominant display technology in premium smartphones. As the technology continues to improve, it is gaining traction in the automotive, IT, and AR/VR markets.

sources.title: ReHome Earth: A VR-Based Concept Validation for AI-Driven Space Homesickness Interventions
sources.abstract: Space exploration has advanced rapidly, but the emotional needs of astronauts on long-duration missions remain underexplored. We present ReHome Earth, a dual-component design approach addressing space homesickness: 1) a future-oriented installation concept integrating transparent OLED displays with spaceship windows for real-time Earth connectivity, and 2) a functional VR prototype simulating astronaut isolation for testing AI-generated content effectiveness. Since accessing astronauts during missions is impossible, we conducted concept validation with terrestrial participants experiencing geographic displacement. Through evaluation with 84 proxy participants and 6 HCI experts, we demonstrate strong emotional resonance and validate three design implications: emotional pacing mechanisms, explainable biophysical feedback systems, and evolution from individual tools to collective affective infrastructure. Our contributions include a technically feasible space installation concept, a functional VR prototype for space HCI research, and empirical insights into the design of AI-driven emotional support systems for extreme isolation environments.

sources.title: Color Calibration Methods For OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Accurate color reproduction on a display requires an inverse display model, mapping colorimetric values (e.g. CIE XYZ) into RGB values driving the display. To create such a model, we collected a large dataset of display color measurements for a high refresh-rate 4-primary OLED display. We demonstrated that, unlike traditional LCD displays, multi-primary OLED display color responses are non-additive and non-linear for some colors. We tested the performances of different regression methods: polynomial regression, look-up tables, multi-layer perceptrons, and others. The best-performing models were additionally validated on newly measured (unseen) test colors. We found that the performances of several variations of 4th-degree polynomial models were comparable to the look-up table and machine-learning-based models while being less resource-intensive.

sources.title: Treat-through OLED Displays: Dosimetry and performance of OLED AVATAR screens for Megavoltage Radiotherapy
sources.abstract: The AVATAR system utilizes a radiolucent video display to help relax and immobilize pediatric patients during radiotherapy. This study investigates the use of OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) displays, which offer superior image quality and faster alignment compared to traditional projector-based systems, albeit with slightly increased thickness. The dose perturbations caused by these screens were assessed to evaluate their suitability for radiotherapy. A 20 cm OLED screen was positioned in the patient's line of sight, between the patient's head and the radiation source. The screen comprises a 0.25 mm thick flexible OLED panel and a custom carbon fiber backing (0.3 to 0.6 mm thick), with most electronic components relocated via ribbon cable. 6 MV portal images were captured with and without the screen to create transmission maps. Additionally, parallel plate ion chamber measurements were taken at the surface and at depth in a solid water phantom. The OLED's radiation tolerance was tested with a 100 Gy dose delivery and 12 months of use in an active radiotherapy linac vault. The portal image transmission maps indicated an average attenuation difference of 0.3\% (SD = 0.37 \%) between measurements with and without the AVATAR screen, with a maximum point attenuation of 3\%. Ion chamber measurements revealed a 0.31\% decrease in dose at 2 cm depth and a 7.04 \% increase at the surface under an anterior-posterior beam. For a VMAT arc, the dose difference was 0.04 \% at 2 cm depth and 0.1\% at the phantom surface. The minimal dose deviations indicate that these screens are suitable for megavoltage arc therapy without significantly affecting the target dose. While surface dose is slightly increased for static anterior beams, it remains low. For lower photon energies or particle beams, larger perturbations may occur, necessitating further measurements or beam entry avoidance.

sources.title: MAX OLED Solution for Next‐Generation OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract A breakthrough in OLED display pixel architecture and manufacturing technology will enhance display performance and enable a wider range of applications.

sources.title: CosmicWatch: The Desktop Muon Detector(v3X)
sources.abstract: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X) is a compact, low-cost, and portable device designed for detecting ionizing radiation, including cosmic-ray muons. Building on previous iterations, the v3X introduces significant hardware and firmware improvements that enhance sensitivity, usability, and data acquisition capabilities. The detector integrates a plastic scintillator and silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), custom designed electronics for signal processing, onboard data storage, OLED display, environmental sensors, and USB connectivity. With a total component cost under \$100 and a build time suitable for high school students, the v3X is ideal for education, outreach, and introductory research applications in particle and astroparticle physics. This paper details the design, performance, and potential use cases of the v3X, supported by example measurements demonstrating its functionality.

sources.title: The application of organic materials used in OLED display
sources.abstract: Based on the advantages of higher luminous efficiency, lower energy consumption and ecological protection, the organic light-emitting diode (OLED) has become a new type of display in mobile OLED device, which was also called as the dream display. Many organic materials including polyimide (PI), photoresist (PR), photosensitive polyimide (PSPI), OLED emissive layer materials, inkjet printing (IJP), optical clear adhesive (OCA) and undercut pixel definition layer (undercut PDL) have been introduced during the manufacturing process of OLED display. The pol less progress (PLP) technology had also been introduced in the OLED display by replacing the polarizer, which also introduced a few new organic materials such as black pixel definition layer (BPDL), black matrix (BM) and color film (CF) and applied in the OLED display. In this paper, the author had a review on the organic materials used in the manufacturing process of an OLED display, which included the application of organic materials used in the array structure, the emissive layer (EL) structure, the display of things (DOT) structure and the new OLED display based on the PLP technology. The application of organic material undercut PDL which was used for forming the protruding spacing columns between pixels to prevent the lateral leakage of current between adjacent pixels was also described detailed in this paper.

sources.title: Modeling and Exploiting the Time Course of Chromatic Adaptation for Display Power Optimizations in Virtual Reality
sources.abstract: We introduce a gaze-tracking--free method to reduce OLED display power consumption in VR with minimal perceptual impact. This technique exploits the time course of chromatic adaptation, the human visual system's ability to maintain stable color perception under changing illumination. To that end, we propose a novel psychophysical paradigm that models how human adaptation state changes with the scene illuminant. We exploit this model to compute an optimal illuminant shift trajectory, controlling the rate and extent of illumination change, to reduce display power under a given perceptual loss budget. Our technique significantly improves the perceptual quality over prior work that applies illumination shifts instantaneously. Our technique can also be combined with prior work on luminance dimming to reduce display power by 31% with no statistical loss of perceptual quality.

sources.title: The Design of a Detection Robot with OLED Display
sources.abstract: OLED display has the advantages of self-illumination, wide viewing angle, fast response, small size, small weight, flexibility. It is a huge breakthrough in the field of display technology, and enhances the visual enjoyment and on-the-spot experience of people. With the rapid development of science and technology, the combination of OLED and robot has attracted attention from most of the fields. In this paper, the working principle, advantages and main application fields of OLED devices are introduced, and a detection robot with OLED is designed. The detection robot can accurately control the speed of the motor and the angle of the steering gear within a distance of 1,000 meters, and receive the images from airborne cameras in real time.

sources.title: IoT-Enabled Smart Car Parking System through Integrated Sensors and Mobile Applications
sources.abstract: Due to more population congestion and car ownership, the provision of parking spaces for vehicles is becoming a crucial factor. This paper aims to present a novel Internet of Things (IoT)--based smart car parking system that can effectively manage these problems with the help of sensor technology and automation. Infrared (IR) sensors, DHT22 sensors, MQ-2 gas sensors, and servo motors are used in the parking space. An OLED display shows the status of parking slots in real-time. Communicating with a mobile application through the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol enables the efficient exchange of data. As a result, this innovative solution optimizes parking space, increases efficiency, and makes the parking lot more comfortable. This IoT system allows real-time monitoring and automation of parked cars as well as fast response to dynamic changes in environmental conditions, setting a new standard for smart parking systems.

sources.title: Polaritons Enable Brilliant Colors in OLED Displays
sources.abstract: Abstract Microcavities can be used to narrow the broad emission spectra of OLED displays—but at the cost of angular dependence. Polaritons solve this issue and enable angle‐independent and highly efficient OLED emissions.

sources.title: STM32-Based Smart Waste Bin for Hygienic Disposal Using Embedded Sensing and Automated Control
sources.abstract: The increasing demand for hygienic and contactless solutions in public and private environments has encouraged the development of automated systems for everyday applications. This paper presents the design and implementation of a motion- sensing automatic waste bin using an STM32 microcontroller, ultrasonic sensors, and a servo motor. The system detects user presence through ultrasonic sensing and automatically opens the bin lid using a servo motor controlled by the microcontroller. An additional ultrasonic sensor is used to monitor the internal waste level of the bin, while an OLED display provides real- time feedback regarding system status. The proposed system offers a low-cost, reliable, and easily deployable solution for touch-free waste disposal. Experimental evaluation demonstrates fast response time, stable sensing performance, and smooth mechanical operation. The system can be effectively deployed in homes, educational institutions, hospitals, and public facilities to improve hygiene and user convenience.

sources.title: Materials to Enable Future OLED Display Evolution
sources.abstract: Abstract Experimental and theoretic approaches will allow for new understandings that are essential to develop OLED materials that enable next‐generation displays.

sources.title: Intrinsic Limitations of Single Layer Polychromatic Metalens for Virtual Reality Visors
sources.abstract: Virtual and augmented reality (VR/AR) visors require compact and lightweight optics. Metalenses have been widely proposed as ultrathin replacements for bulky refractive eyepieces, with performance typically assessed using point spread function (PSF) and modulation transfer function (MTF) measurements. Here, we design, fabricate, and characterize a single-layer silicon nitride metalens optimized for the three emission peaks of an RGB OLED display, and benchmark it against refractive and Fresnel eyepieces. Under coherent illumination, the metalens exhibits a tightly confined PSF and strong mid-to-high spatial-frequency MTF, suggesting excellent optical performance. However, when evaluated in a realistic system-level VR testbed incorporating incoherent OLED illumination, a dynamic-pupil eye model, and near-eye-relevant focal lengths, the same device exhibits pronounced ghosting and background haze. We show that these artifacts arise from the intrinsic multifocal nature of polychromatic diffractive focusing and demonstrate that common mitigation strategies such as narrowband filtering and long-focal-length relay optics merely mask, rather than resolve, the issue. Our results establish that meta-optics for AR/VR must be evaluated under realistic system-level conditions to reveal their true imaging performance.

sources.title: OLED lifetime simulation for VR displays
sources.abstract: This paper introduces a new methodology for simulating the burn-in of an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) microdisplay used in a virtual reality (VR) headset. The proposed simulation employs the stretched exponential decay (SED) model, which is widely used to predict the degradation of the OLED device over time. Furthermore, the model integrates the impact of user head motion on VR display image content. The study defines productivity and gaming mode surrogate image content from which to simulate burn-in and applies image processing correlating to head motion data collected from a user study. The results of this study indicate that head motion has a significant impact on OLED burn-in. Given a conservative assumption for image content and head motion, the time for visual failure due to burn-in artifacts is 4 times slower than a case with stationary image content.

sources.title: Solution-processed OLEDs for printing displays
sources.abstract: Recent advances in solution-processed organic light-emitting diodes toward printing displays are reviewed in terms of light-emitting materials, devices, printing techniques and applications.

sources.title: Electrically driven organic laser using integrated OLED pumping
sources.abstract: Abstract Organic semiconductors are carbon-based materials that combine optoelectronic properties with simple fabrication and the scope for tuning by changing their chemical structure1–3. They have been successfully used to make organic light-emitting diodes2,4,5 (OLEDs, now widely found in mobile phone displays and televisions), solar cells1, transistors6 and sensors7. However, making electrically driven organic semiconductor lasers is very challenging8,9. It is difficult because organic semiconductors typically support only low current densities, suffer substantial absorption from injected charges and triplets, and have additional losses due to contacts10,11. In short, injecting charges into the gain medium leads to intolerable losses. Here we take an alternative approach in which charge injection and lasing are spatially separated, thereby greatly reducing losses. We achieve this by developing an integrated device structure that efficiently couples an OLED, with exceptionally high internal-light generation, with a polymer distributed feedback laser. Under the electrical driving of the integrated structure, we observe a threshold in light output versus drive current, with a narrow emission spectrum and the formation of a beam above the threshold. These observations confirm lasing. Our results provide an organic electronic device that has not been previously demonstrated, and show that indirect electrical pumping by an OLED is a very effective way of realizing an electrically driven organic semiconductor laser. This provides an approach to visible lasers that could see applications in spectroscopy, metrology and sensing.

sources.title: P‐14.14: IJP OLEDs Advanced Adaptive De‐burn‐in algorithm
sources.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
sources.abstract: We propose a solution to IS (Image Sticking), one of the important issue in IJPOLEDs , which has various advantages over conventional vacuum deposition methods. One solution to IS is De‐burn‐in technology (DBI), but it cannot be completely improved due to deviation in OLED life characteristics. In addition, managing variations in the life characteristics mentioned above is required to ensure that DBI performance is sufficient. To solve this problem, we propose a method of DBI design based on variability. By performing a short life evaluation and measuring the initial optical characteristics of each panel during the manufacturing stage, DBI settings were implemented individually. This allows for a wide range of characteristic to be resolved. In fact, we constructed a manufacturing method, and through the introduction of the architecture, the difference in brightness due to deterioration was reduced to less than 1/3.

sources.title: Bimolecular Annihilation Processes in OLEDs
sources.abstract: This thesis investigates the physical limitations and efficiency roll-off of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) at high brightness levels. Due to the low dielectric constant of organic semiconductors, tightly bound excitons are formed, which at high current densities trigger bimolecular loss mechanisms such as triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA) and triplet–polaron annihilation (TPA). These phenomena reduce device efficiency and generate heat as well as high-energy excited states, which cause chemical damage to the materials and shorten the operational lifespan of the device. The study demonstrates that these losses can be managed by restricting exciton diffusion through host–guest systems or by accelerating radiative recombination using optical microcavities. The development of OLED devices requires a constant balance between high efficiency, durability, and manufacturing complexity. Future research should focus particularly on improving the stability of blue emitters and developing more precise kinetic models to ensure the reliability of mass-produced devices.

sources.title: Recent research on the status and advances of OLED
sources.abstract: Organic Light-Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) have already been a prominent display technology in various applications for many decades, ranging from smartphones and televisions to wearable devices and lighting. It is important to understand the current state of OLED research in order to assess its progress, identify challenges, and explore more potential ways for further development. In this paper, the significance and widespread adoption of OLED technology are briefly introduced, and its advantages over traditional display technologies are highlighted. The paper then provides a concise overview of the major components and working principles of OLEDs without delving into basic notions. The paper discusses both small molecule OLEDs (SMOLEDs) and polymer OLEDs (POLEDs), emphasizing their unique structure, characteristics and properties. Different strategies employed to enhance OLED performance is investigated, including the regulation of band gaps that influence the efficiency and brightness. This paper also focuses on the evaluation of device reliability and stability aspects. The techniques and materials employed in studies related to OLED development are also discussed with many searched experimental data and ongoing research activities. Furthermore, the research content covered the aspects of recent commercial advancements in OLED technology, such as Active matrix OLEDs (AMOLED) and Passive matrix (PMOLED). The review provides a guideline for researchers, industry professionals, and enthusiasts to better understand the OLED technology into its details, potential, and the areas that require further exploration.

sources.title: 46.1: Invited Paper: LCD Innovations vs. OLED Performance for Automotive Applications
sources.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers
sources.abstract: LCDs are today's workhorse for automotive displays. In recent years, some premium OEMs started to ship cars with OLED displays. The advantages of OLEDs compared to LCDs are short response time at low temperature (relevant for e‐mirrors) and perfect black at night as well as highly curved and transparent versions. Replacing edge‐lit backlight of LCDs by FALD (full array local dimming) results in highest luminance at acceptable halo. Furthermore, LCDs have a large supply chain, which results in competitive cost. Well‐known challenges of OLEDs deal with high luminance and temperature sensitivity, which can result in reduced lifetime (LT) incl. Burn‐In. Challenges and solutions for LCDs and OLEDs such as halo measurements and viewing angle performance will be discussed more in detail. Latest automotive demonstrators show the potential of micro‐LEDs and electrically pumped Quantum Dots (QD) displays. Both have the potential to outperform LCDs and OLEDs.

sources.title: Hyperphosphorescent OLEDs: Harnessing the Power of MR‐TADF Terminal Emitters
sources.abstract: Abstract Hyperphosphorescent organic light‐emitting diodes (HP‐OLEDs) represent an attractive solution to persistent efficiency roll‐off and device stability issues, combining phosphorescent sensitizers with fluorescent terminal emitters to achieve efficient, narrowband emission. This review discusses advances in HP‐OLEDs where the terminal emitter is a multiresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence compound. Recent breakthroughs in device performance, including examples demonstrating both high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max ) and excellent color purity, are highlighted. This review summarizes design strategies, challenges, and future directions for improving the efficiency, stability, and spectral performance of HP‐OLEDs.

sources.title: Research Progress on the Preparation of OLED Based on the Inkjet Printing
sources.abstract: Abstract Over the past few decades, organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) have demonstrated compelling technological advantages due to their ability to directly convert electrons into photons without requiring backlighting, thereby offering self‐emissive surfaces, ultrathin device profiles, compatibility with flexible substrates, high luminance, and exceptional contrast ratios (achieving true black). Today, OLEDs dominate the market for small‐scale displays such as smartphones and laptops. Propelled by the burgeoning ubiquity of the Internet of Things, OLEDs are poised to experience an exponential upsurge in prospective exigency. However, conventional thermal evaporation techniques face challenges in achieving uniform large‐area OLED fabrication, rendering mass production costly and complex—a persistent drawback hindering OLEDs from becoming the undisputed market leader. Amidst this milieu, inkjet printing (IJP) has magnetized considerable scholarly and commercial traction across the panoply of fabrication modalities, crystallizing as the pre‐eminent candidate for scalable, large‐area OLED manufacturing. This technique boasts non‐contact processing, high material utilization, and compatibility with roll‐to‐roll manufacturing. In this review, the critical parameters governing ink formulation are delineated and provide an overview of prevailing OLED device architectures. Subsequently, recent advancements are consolidate in inkjet‐printed OLED layers, culminating in a circumspect prognosis of the extant impediments and the prospective trajectory toward wholly inkjet‐patterned OLED architectures.

sources.title: The Effect of Molecular Structure on the Properties of Fluorene Derivatives for OLED Applications
sources.abstract: A new family of symmetrical fluorene derivatives with different types of substituents attached to the C-2 and C-7 positions of the fluorene core synthesized by the Sonogashira coupling reactions is reported. The electronic structures and the properties of the compounds investigated by means of photoelectron emission spectroscopy, UV-Vis absorption and photoluminescent spectroscopy as well as by DFT and TD-DFT theoretical calculations are discussed. It is shown that the nature of substituents influences the π-conjugation of the molecules. No intermolecular charge transfer within the investigated wavelength range is observed. The applicability of the synthesized compounds in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) based on exciplex emission is demonstrated. The advanced co-deposition technique with the tuned OLED architecture was applied and resulted in improved OLED parameters.

sources.title: Treat-through OLED Displays: Dosimetry and performance of OLED AVATAR screens for Megavoltage Radiotherapy
sources.abstract: The AVATAR system utilizes a radiolucent video display to help relax and immobilize pediatric patients during radiotherapy. This study investigates the use of OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) displays, which offer superior image quality and faster alignment compared to traditional projector-based systems, albeit with slightly increased thickness. The dose perturbations caused by these screens were assessed to evaluate their suitability for radiotherapy. A 20 cm OLED screen was positioned in the patient's line of sight, between the patient's head and the radiation source. The screen comprises a 0.25 mm thick flexible OLED panel and a custom carbon fiber backing (0.3 to 0.6 mm thick), with most electronic components relocated via ribbon cable. 6 MV portal images were captured with and without the screen to create transmission maps. Additionally, parallel plate ion chamber measurements were taken at the surface and at depth in a solid water phantom. The OLED's radiation tolerance was tested with a 100 Gy dose delivery and 12 months of use in an active radiotherapy linac vault. The portal image transmission maps indicated an average attenuation difference of 0.3\% (SD = 0.37 \%) between measurements with and without the AVATAR screen, with a maximum point attenuation of 3\%. Ion chamber measurements revealed a 0.31\% decrease in dose at 2 cm depth and a 7.04 \% increase at the surface under an anterior-posterior beam. For a VMAT arc, the dose difference was 0.04 \% at 2 cm depth and 0.1\% at the phantom surface. The minimal dose deviations indicate that these screens are suitable for megavoltage arc therapy without significantly affecting the target dose. While surface dose is slightly increased for static anterior beams, it remains low. For lower photon energies or particle beams, larger perturbations may occur, necessitating further measurements or beam entry avoidance.

sources.title: Vacuum Thermal Evaporation for OLEDs: Fundamentals, Optimization, and Implications for Perovskite LEDs
sources.abstract: Abstract Organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) are central to high‐end displays and solid‐state lighting due to their small thickness and high flexibility, wide color gamut, and low power consumption. While solution processing offers simplicity and cost advantages for polymer‐based OLEDs, vacuum thermal evaporation (VTE) remains the dominant method for the commercial production of high‐performance small‐molecule OLEDs, owing to its precise control over film thickness, material purity, and multilayer integration. However, to meet the demands of display applications for higher performance, lower cost and more diverse forms (such as flexibility and high resolution), it is crucial to continuously optimize the VTE process. Meanwhile, although solution processing remains the predominant approach for perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs), recent exploratory efforts have investigated VTE as an alternative route, thereby opening opportunities to transfer process insights from OLEDs to PeLEDs. This review aims to systematically summarize the application foundation and optimization strategies of VTE technology in OLEDs, and to explore how these mature practices can inform the process development and device design of vacuum‐evaporated PeLEDs.

findings.claim: Burn-in, image sticking and lifetime degradation remain unresolved reliability risks for OLED displays. This holds across consumer, automotive, VR and inkjet-printed (IJP) panels, and compensation methods only partly mitigate it.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: Two abstracts (SID conference papers) name lifetime and burn-in as known challenges. The IJP paper says de-burn-in (DBI) cannot be fully improved because of panel-to-panel variation in lifetime. Neither abstract gives lifetime figures, so the size of the problem is not quantified here.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Well‐known challenges of OLEDs deal with high luminance and temperature sensitivity, which can result in reduced lifetime (LT) incl. Burn‐In.

findings.claim: Physical efficiency limits at high brightness create a trade-off between efficiency, durability and manufacturing complexity. Bimolecular annihilation generates heat and damaging excited states, and blue emitter stability is still named as an open problem.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The source is a university thesis, which is not a standard peer-reviewed journal paper. A review of hyperphosphorescent OLEDs (HP-OLEDs) likewise describes efficiency roll-off and stability as 'persistent' issues. Both are abstract-only, and the thesis proposes mitigations without quantifying them.
findings.supporting_excerpt: These phenomena reduce device efficiency and generate heat as well as high-energy excited states, which cause chemical damage to the materials and shorten the operational lifespan of the device.

findings.claim: Large-area, low-cost OLED manufacturing is not yet solved. Vacuum thermal evaporation (VTE) is the dominant commercial process but is described as costly and complex at large area. Inkjet printing is promoted as the alternative, yet the IJP paper in this set still reports lifetime-variability problems.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: One review says evaporation struggles with uniform large-area fabrication, rendering mass production costly and complex. Another says VTE 'remains the dominant method' for high-performance small-molecule OLEDs. The IJP image-sticking paper reports lifetime deviations that complicate de-burn-in. The abstracts give no yield, cost-per-panel or throughput data, so it is a gap whether IJP can match VTE performance and cost. The timing is my inference, not stated in the abstracts. The solution-processing review abstract is too brief to assess.

findings.claim: OLEDs face competition from LCDs and possibly micro-LED or electrically pumped QD displays. In automotive use, LCDs with full-array local dimming (FALD) are cited as having a large supply chain and competitive cost.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This rests on a single invited conference abstract focused on automotive. Its claim that micro-LED and QD 'have the potential to outperform' OLEDs is prospective and not backed by data in the abstract. Whether alternatives displace OLED in other segments is a gap.
findings.supporting_excerpt: LCDs have a large supply chain, which results in competitive cost.

findings.claim: The VR burn-in lifetime evidence is simulation-only. It relies on the stretched exponential decay model and surrogate image content, so the reported 4x slower visual failure under head motion may not transfer to real headsets.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstract describes a simulation using a widely used degradation model, 'productivity and gaming mode surrogate image content' and head-motion data from a user study. It states a 'conservative assumption' for content and motion. The paper has 0 citations and no independent replication in this set. The result is relative to stationary content, not an absolute lifetime, and VR use may still carry burn-in risk where content is static (for example UI elements). This is my inference.

findings.claim: Several results in this set are lab-scale or narrow demonstrations and say little about commercial display risk or readiness. These include the electrically driven organic laser, the fluorene-derivative exciplex OLEDs and the radiotherapy screen.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The Nature organic-laser paper is a proof-of-concept and its abstract lists the underlying difficulties: low current densities and charge/triplet absorption losses. The fluorene paper reports 'improved OLED parameters' without numbers in the abstract. The radiotherapy paper is an arXiv preprint (not peer reviewed) from one setup with a 20 cm screen, and it reports a 7.04% surface-dose increase. None of these addresses display-market viability, and the abstracts give no scale-up evidence.

hype_flags: 'Exponential upsurge in prospective exigency' for OLED demand driven by IoT (src_1ae66a9e98): the abstract is promotional and gives no demand data.

Inkjet printing as 'the pre-eminent candidate' for scalable large-area OLED production (src_1ae66a9e98): review framing, with no yield or cost evidence in the abstract, while another paper in the set still reports lifetime-variability problems.
Micro-LED and electrically pumped QD displays 'have the potential to outperform' LCD and OLED (src_125ddf53dd): a prospective statement with no supporting data in the abstract.
Electrically driven organic laser (src_bc1460208b): a scientific milestone that should not be read as near-term display relevance.
'Superior image quality and faster alignment' of OLED over projector systems in radiotherapy (src_dc5ddf0cb0): a single-site preprint, not a general market signal.

finding.claim: S6 credits the 31% VR display power saving to the illuminant-shift trajectory method. The abstract attributes 31% to the technique combined with prior luminance dimming. The trajectory method's own share is not given in the abstract. The result also comes from a single preprint and a psychophysical study with an unreported sample size.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The 31% figure applies to a combined approach, not to the chromatic-adaptation trajectory alone as S6 states. "No statistically significant loss" in a limited perceptual study is also not the same as no loss, and it is not peer-reviewed.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Our technique can also be combined with prior work on luminance dimming to reduce display power by 31% with no statistical loss of perceptual quality.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S1 presents blue PHOLED lifetime as largely solved. The source says lifetimes are "approaching" green analogs, not matching them, and it is a single perspective article that also lists remaining challenges. A 2026 thesis in the retrieved set still names blue emitter stability as a priority for future work. The abstract gives no numbers, device conditions or commercial-readiness criteria.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The finding rests on one author-written perspective abstract with no quantitative lifetimes. "Approaching" does not mean adoption-grade stability. The abstract's own wording ("challenges and opportunities confronting further development") and src_8078af2390 ("improving the stability of blue emitters") suggest the problem is not closed. The label verified_fact is too strong for the implied conclusion.

finding.claim: S2 mixes up two statements. The abstract says blue pixels consume about 50% of front-plane energy, and that PHOLEDs specifically had not met stability standards. S2 attributes both to "blue OLED emitters" in general, which implies no blue emitter is usable. The abstract does not say this. The sentence is also garbled, since emitters do not consume the energy. The 25 years refers to the time since PHOLEDs were invented.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The excerpt restricts the 25-year problem to 100%-internal-efficiency PHOLEDs, not to all blue OLED emitters. Scope and wording need correcting.
finding.supporting_excerpt: in the 25 years since their invention, 100% internal efficiency phosphorescent OLEDs (PHOLEDs) have not met the stability standards necessary for their adoption.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S5 generalises to "multi-primary OLED displays" from a dataset measured on one high-refresh-rate 4-primary OLED display. The finding that fourth-degree polynomials match look-up-table and ML accuracy was validated only on that panel's unseen colours. It may not carry over to other panels, primary counts or ageing states, and the abstract gives no error figures.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: A single-device dataset limits how far the non-additivity and model-comparison conclusions can be generalised. Panel-to-panel variation is not addressed in the abstract.
finding.supporting_excerpt: we collected a large dataset of display color measurements for a high refresh-rate 4-primary OLED display.
finding.guard_note: relabelled ai_interpretation: a challenge is a judgement; its quoted excerpt was checked against the source

finding.claim: S7 calls the dose perturbations "small" while including a 7.04% surface dose increase and a 3% maximum point attenuation. A surface dose change of that size can matter clinically for skin dose. This is a single preprint. The abstract is cut off before the survival and other results, so the 100 Gy and 12-month tolerance claim is not visible in the text provided. The topic is also peripheral to OLED display technology.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: "Small" is a judgement that the abstract does not make, and it depends on the clinical threshold. The abstract reports a 7.04% surface increase and a maximum point attenuation of 3%. The panel-survival claim cannot be checked from the truncated abstract and the preprint is not peer-reviewed.

finding.claim: S8 treats the physics-constrained MeshGraphNet as a validated predictor of OLED panel drop-impact response. The abstract describes a surrogate model trained on simulated ball-drop data, in a preprint, with no stated experimental validation on physical panels. The abstract's generalisation test is cut off, so the claimed robustness cannot be assessed. The result concerns mechanical modelling, not OLED display performance.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The abstract speaks of "dynamic physics simulations" and a "validated model" without naming physical test data. Better stability from relative-displacement prediction is shown only in the model's own setting. The label verified_fact overstates what the abstract supports.

finding.claim: S10 draws a broad conclusion, that materials and pixel architecture are the main levers for next-stage OLED evolution, and lists specific materials and structures. Almost all the specifics come from one review abstract (src_b611624276). The other two cited sources have one-sentence abstracts that name none of them. The finding thus looks like triangulation across sources while resting on one.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: The excerpt from src_2f6b4e2c44 is generic and names no PLP, IJP or PDL items. The "multiple sources" framing overstates convergence. The "main levers" ranking is also not tested against other levers, such as emitter stability or driving and compensation schemes.
finding.supporting_excerpt: Experimental and theoretic approaches will allow for new understandings that are essential to develop OLED materials that enable next‐generation displays.

limitations: Only titles and abstracts were available (text_depth abstract_only). Several abstracts are truncated or very short, such as the solution-processed OLED review.

Only 12 papers were provided, several off-topic for display investment risk (radiotherapy screens, organic laser, fluorene synthesis, perovskite LED crossover). No data on pricing, supply chain, capex, yield or market share were present.

The sources are mostly reviews and conference abstracts, with few independent replications. The arXiv radiotherapy item is a preprint and not peer reviewed, and the thesis is not a standard journal paper.
Several of the lifetime and burn-in results lack quantitative figures in the abstracts, so the severity of reliability problems versus current commercial practice cannot be judged.

The set contains no papers on specific competing technologies (micro-LED, QD-OLED, LCD mini-LED) beyond one automotive abstract. Competitive risk is therefore under-covered, and absence here is a coverage gap, not evidence of low risk.

Only titles and abstracts were available. Some abstracts are truncated, and several Information Display items are one-sentence blurbs. Challenges rest on what the abstracts do and do not state, not on full-text checks.
I did not independently search for papers that rebut the blue PHOLED lifetime claims beyond the retrieved set. The absence of contradicting evidence is not evidence that none exists.

S3, S4, S9, S11 and S12 appear consistent with their cited abstracts, and I left them unchallenged. S4 and S9 are low-stakes and hedged. S11 is accurately summarised, although it concerns metalens optics rather than OLED panels.
I did not assess commercial or market claims, and nothing here is investment advice.

sources.title: Passivation repairing method of ITO sputtering target material for preparing silicon-based Micro-OLED and application of passivation repairing method [CN122648888A]
authors: SHANGHAI BETONE SEMICONDUCTOR ENERGY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SHANGHAI BETONE SEMICONDUCTOR ENERGY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention provides a passivation repairing method of an ITO sputtering target material for preparing a silicon-based Micro-OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) and application of the passivation repairing method. The passivation repairing method comprises the steps that standby state parameters of the ITO target material are obtained, and the passivation level of the surface of the ITO target material is judged according to the standby state parameters; the passivation layer comprises a loose adsorption pollution layer and a polarization high-resistance insulating layer from outside to inside; in an oxygen-free environment, a loose adsorption pollution layer of the ITO target material is removed by adopting a physical stripping mode, and then a reverse negative-pressure pulse electric field is applied to perform depolarization treatment on the polarized high-resistance insulating layer; monitoring a discharge state feedback parameter of the ITO target material in real time so as to dynamically adjust a pulse sputtering parameter; and carrying out steady-state sputtering deposition on the ITO thin film so as to form the ITO anode layer of the silicon-based Micro-OLED. According to the invention, the complete resetting of the target material state and the high stability of the sputtering process are realized, and reliable guarantee is provided for the high-performance preparation of the silicon-based Micro-OLED.

sources.title: SOURCE-SIDE SYNCHRONIZATION OF FRAME UPDATES FOR DISPLAYS [US20260229193A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems and methods for source-side variable refresh rate (VRR) synchronization for organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays are described. A processor may determine a number of emission cycles since a previous frame update based on emission cycle information of a display. The processor may determine a time delay based on the number of emission cycles and may provide a next frame to the display based on the time delay to align the next frame with an emission cycle boundary of the display. The time delay may be determined based on whether the number of emission cycles is an integer and whether the number of emission cycles is less than a number of emission cycles per frame. Source-side synchronization may enable VRR operation on OLED displays without requiring frame buffer hardware in the display timing controller.

A first organic light-emitting (OLE) material is disposed over the first anode. A first cathode is disposed over the first OLE material. The first cathode contacts the first overhang structure. The first overhang structure is electrically coupled to the first busbar. A second sub-pixel is bounded by a third overhang structure and a fourth overhang structure. The second sub-pixel includes a second anode. A second organic light-emitting (OLE) material is disposed over the second anode. A second cathode is disposed over the second OLE material. The second cathode contacts the third overhang structure. The third overhang structure is electrically coupled to the second busbar.

sources.title: Pixel unit, display panel and display device [CN122341049A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of semiconductors, and discloses a pixel unit, a display panel and a display device.The pixel unit comprises a first color pixel region, a second color pixel region and a third color pixel region, the pixel unit comprises an organic light-emitting layer, a color filter layer and a lens layer which are arranged in a stacked mode, and the lens layer comprises a lens structure; the lens structure comprises a first lens structure corresponding to the first color pixel area, a second lens structure corresponding to the second color pixel area and a third lens structure corresponding to the third color pixel area; each lens structure comprises a first lens part, a second lens part and a third lens part which are arranged in a stacked mode and sequentially communicated, the top of each first lens part is a first curved surface protruding in the direction away from the substrate, each second lens part is of a columnar structure arranged in the direction of the light path, and the bottom face of each third lens part is a second curved surface protruding in the direction of the substrate. The pixel unit can be well matched with a micro OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) miniaturized pixel structure, and the light emitting intensity and the light efficiency of the pixel unit are effectively improved.

sources.title: SUBSTRATE CLEANING LIQUID, METHOD FOR PRODUCING SUBSTRATE CLEANED USING SAME, AND METHOD FOR PRODUCING DEVICE [WO2026139475A1]
sources.abstract: [Problem] To obtain a substrate cleaning liquid capable of cleaning a substrate and removing particles. [Solution] A substrate cleaning liquid comprising a hydrophobic polymer (A), a polar compound (B), and a solvent (C): wherein the polar compound (B) is soluble in water. The substrate cleaning liquid is a highly functional material that can be used in a semiconductor device production step of a nanotechnology process, for example, a step of producing a semiconductor device that controls liquid crystals, quantum dots, or OLED displays formed on a substrate.

sources.title: COMPOSITION, MANUFACTURING METHOD OF CURED FILM, MANUFACTURING METHOD OF ELECTRONIC ELEMENT, AND USE OF COMPOSITION [WO2026139452A1]
sources.abstract: To provide a composition comprising a polysilazane. A manufacturing method according to the present invention may be used with a nanotechnology process to manufacture applications of semiconductor devices and display devices. For example, liquid crystals, quantum dots, or OLED displays formed on a substrate can be manufactured, and these may be controlled by a semiconductor. The preferred performance of the manufacturing method according to the present invention may be supported by at least one of the properties of high-performance materials and advanced materials. A composition comprising a polysilazane, at least one of a unit A represented by Formula (1A) or a unit B represented by Formula (1B), and a solvent.

sources.title: Micro-OLED defect detection jig [CN224436137U]
authors: NINGBO HONGYI PHOTOELECTRIC TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: NINGBO HONGYI PHOTOELECTRIC TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The utility model discloses a jig for Micro-OLED defect detection, which belongs to the technical field of work fixtures and comprises a vacuum seat, an insulating seat and a cover plate, the insulating seat is arranged on the vacuum seat, a groove is arranged at the edge of one side of the insulating seat, an OLED flexible flat cable bearing seat is arranged in the groove, an OLED flexible flat cable positioning groove is arranged on the OLED flexible flat cable bearing seat, and the OLED flexible flat cable positioning groove is arranged on the OLED flexible flat cable bearing seat. One end of the cover plate is hinged with one end of the insulating seat, the other end of the cover plate is clamped with the other end of the insulating seat, the cover plate is provided with a probe seat at a position corresponding to the OLED flexible flat cable bearing seat, the top of the cover plate is provided with a control circuit board, and the control circuit board is electrically connected with a probe on the probe seat. The device is simple in structure and convenient to use, the consistency of workpiece placement is guaranteed, the OLED to be tested can be rapidly lightened, golden fingers of OLED flexible flat cables cannot be damaged, the qualified rate of products is guaranteed, the workpieces are also convenient to disassemble and assemble, and the working efficiency is greatly improved.

sources.title: Preparation method of Micro-OLED structure with high luminous efficiency [CN122294750A]
authors: ANHUI XINSHIJIA SEMICONDUCTOR DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: ANHUI XINSHIJIA SEMICONDUCTOR DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a preparation method of a Micro-OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) structure with high luminous efficiency, relates to the technical field of OLED display, and aims to prepare a silicon dioxide/silicon nitride double-layer dielectric layer on a CMOS (Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor) substrate in order to solve the problems of insufficient brightness, serious loss of large-angle scattered light and bottleneck in luminous efficiency improvement of the existing silicon-based Micro-OLED. A parabola curved surface reflection bowl anode is prepared by utilizing the etching rate difference of the two layers, the preparation of a pixel definition layer, an organic light-emitting layer, a thin film packaging layer, a color filter layer and a flat layer is completed in sequence, and finally a micro-lens array coaxially corresponding to the reflection bowl is prepared to form a collaborative condensation system. According to the invention, the internal optical loss of the device can be greatly reduced, the peak brightness and the light emitting efficiency are remarkably improved, the existing mass production process is compatible, and the highlight application requirement of AR/VR near-to-eye display is met.

sources.title: Display panel, display screen and electronic equipment [CN122294732A]
sources.abstract: The embodiment of the invention provides a display panel, a display screen and electronic equipment, and relates to the technical field of electronic equipment. The display panel comprises a pixel definition layer and a light emitting layer. An opening is formed in the pixel definition layer in a surrounding mode, a supporting body is arranged on the surface of the pixel definition layer, a charge generation layer and a cathode layer are arranged on the surface of the supporting body, the surface of the pixel definition layer and in the opening in a stacked mode, and the light-emitting layer is arranged in the opening. The display panel is provided with an isolation groove, the isolation groove is wound on the outer side of the supporting body, the display panel is provided with an isolation area located on the inner side of the isolation groove and a functional area located on the outer side of the isolation groove, the supporting body is located in the isolation area, and the light-emitting layer is located in the functional area. The isolation groove penetrates through at least one of the cathode layer and the charge generation layer in the thickness direction of the display panel, so that the portions, on the two sides of the isolation groove, of at least one of the cathode layer and the charge generation layer are disconnected. Therefore, the Tandem OLED display panel is not easy to have the problems of low brightness, bright spots and the like due to the damage of the structural layer on the surface of the support body.

sources.title: SILOXANE COMPOUND, COMPOSITION COMPRISING SILOXANE COMPOUND, METHOD FOR PRODUCING CURED FILM, CURED FILM, AND ELECTRONIC DEVICE [WO2026131608A1]
sources.abstract: [Problem] To provide a siloxane compound. The production method according to the present invention produces applications for semiconductor devices and display devices, and thus may be used with nano-technology processes. For example, the method can produce liquid crystal, quantum dots, or OLED displays formed on substrates, which can be controlled with semiconductors. Preferred performance of the production method according to the invention may be supported by at least one of the properties of high-performance materials and advanced materials. [Means of Solution] A siloxane compound having a siloxane bonding degree of 0.25 to 0.885, preferably 0.40 to 0.875, more preferably 0.50 to 0.86, still more preferably 0.60 to 0.85 and even more preferably 0.70 to 0.82.

sources.title: Pixel definition layer, Micro OLED panel and preparation method thereof [CN122248927A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a pixel definition layer, which comprises a first material layer formed by a first material, a second material layer formed by a second material, a third material layer formed by a third material, a fourth material layer formed by a fourth material and a fifth material layer formed by a fifth material, the first material layer, the second material layer, the third material layer, the fourth material layer and the fifth material layer are sequentially arranged, and the thicknesses of the first material layer, the second material layer, the third material layer, the fourth material layer and the fifth material layer are all smaller than 100 nm. The pixel definition layer is formed by stacking five layers of nano films, so that the effect of reducing the reflection of the anode metal layer is achieved, and the reflection of the Micro OLED panel can be reduced. The invention further discloses a Micro OLED panel and a preparation method of the Micro OLED panel.

sources.title: Preparation method of color filter, color filter and Micro OLED panel [CN122180290A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a preparation method of a color filter. The preparation method comprises the following steps: S1, providing a glass wafer; s2, forming a first covering layer on one side of the glass wafer; s3, forming a colored glue layer on one side, far away from the glass wafer, of the first covering layer; wherein in the step S1, the glass wafer is formed by aluminum oxide, the glass wafer comprises a substrate layer and a lens arranged on the substrate layer, and the substrate layer and the lens are integrally formed. According to the preparation method of the color filter, the technological process can be simplified, the production efficiency and the productivity can be improved, and the product thickness of a Micro OLED panel can be reduced. The invention further discloses a color filter and a Micro OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) panel.

sources.title: Silicon-based OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) micro-display device glue curing device, curing method and Micro OLED [CN122164636A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a glue curing device for a silicon-based OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) micro display device. Comprising a lamp set module, an illumination detection module located below the lamp set module and used for collecting irradiation data, a lamp set rotation driving device used for controlling the lamp set module to conduct 360-degree rotation irradiation, and a control system electrically connected with the illumination detection module and the lamp set rotation driving device. According to the glue curing device for the silicon-based OLED micro-display device, the curing uniformity of each area in the curing process of the cover plate glass and substrate attaching glue can be effectively improved. The invention further discloses a glue curing method of the silicon-based OLED micro display device and a Micro OLED.

sources.title: Through hole packaging structure, LTPO display screen and LTPS display screen [CN122094358A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a through hole packaging structure, an LTPO display screen and an LTPS display screen, and relates to the technical field of display screen hole sealing, the through hole packaging structure comprises a substrate, a drilling and carving structure is formed above the substrate, and a plurality of gaps are formed in the drilling and carving structure through etching; the drilling and carving structure comprises an inorganic substance layer and a metal layer which are stacked from bottom to top; a first supporting structure, a second supporting structure and a third supporting structure are further formed above the drilling and carving structure. The method has the beneficial effects that the stacked structure of the metal and the inorganic material is adopted, and the etching rate of the metal and the inorganic material is different, so that the drilling and etching structure is formed by lateral etching, and compared with the drilling and etching stacked structure formed by a traditional mode of stacking an organic layer and an inorganic layer, the method has a better through hole packaging effect. According to the flexible through hole packaging structure, the metal layer is added on the original connecting hole layer, and the etching rate of metal and inorganic materials is different, so that the drilling and etching stacked structure can be formed through lateral etching, and the manufacturing process can be simplified.

sources.title: Silicon-based OLED display screen and anode and preparation method thereof [CN122069916A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a low-electric-leakage and high-color-gamut Micro OLED display screen anode, a preparation method thereof and a low-electric-leakage and high-color-gamut Micro OLED display screen, and belongs to the technical field of semiconductor devices. The Micro OLED display screen anode with low electric leakage and high color gamut comprises a silicon substrate, a pixel insulating layer, anode metal and an organic light-emitting layer. A pixel insulating layer is additionally arranged between anode metal and a silicon substrate, a conductive column is embedded in the pixel insulating layer, the width of the pixel insulating layer is consistent with the size of the anode metal, the conductive column is connected with metal in the silicon substrate and is consistent with the size of a through hole, the anode metal is lifted through the pixel insulating layer, the depth of a PDL central channel is increased, and the thickness of the PDL central channel is increased. The problem of slight electric leakage between sub-pixel anodes is solved, it is guaranteed that when a Micro OLED product is lightened in a single-color mode, sub-pixels of other colors do not emit light slightly, and the color gamut of the lightened product is improved.

sources.title: Display panel and display device [CN122069910A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of Micro OLED display, and discloses a display panel and a display device.The display panel comprises light-emitting units arranged in an array and light filtering units in one-to-one correspondence with the light-emitting units, and the light filtering units have preset offset relative to the light-emitting units; the light filtering unit comprises a first light filter, a second light filter and a third light filter which are different in color; the third optical filter comprises a first sub-optical filter and a second sub-optical filter which are different in color, and the first sub-optical filter is adjacent to the first optical filter and the second optical filter; and the color of the first sub-optical filter is the same as that of the first optical filter, or the color of the first sub-optical filter is the same as that of the second optical filter, or any one of black or structural color. According to the invention, the brightness secondary peak in the anti-CRA direction caused by the offset of the optical filter can be effectively inhibited, the uniformity of the visual angle brightness of the display panel is improved, the adverse effect of anti-CRA stray light on the imaging quality is eliminated, the optical defects such as color cast and ghost images are avoided, and the process is simple.

sources.title: Micro-OLED chip packaging structure, packaging method and Micro-OLED display device [CN122054858A]
authors: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: SEMICONDUCTOR INTEGRATED DISPLAY TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a Micro-OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) chip packaging structure, a Micro-OLED chip packaging method and a Micro-OLED display device. The packaging structure comprises a semiconductor wafer which is provided with a conductive through hole penetrating to a metal bonding pad on the front surface of the semiconductor wafer; the plurality of metal bumps are formed on the back surface of the semiconductor wafer and are electrically connected with the metal bonding pads on the front surface through the conductive through holes and the metal rewiring layer on the back surface; the Micro-OLED light emitting layer is formed on the front surface of the semiconductor wafer; and the transparent cover plate is bonded with the front surface of the semiconductor wafer through a supporting wall. According to the invention, the wafer-level chip size packaging process sequence of the Micro-OLED is optimized as follows: the through holes and the salient points are firstly manufactured on the back surface, and then the OLED is manufactured on the front surface. According to the method, the metal bonding pads are allowed to be led out from the two sides, three sides or four sides of the chip, and particularly, the large-current power supply/ground bonding pads are arranged at the four corners of the chip, so that the internal current distribution of the chip is remarkably optimized, the IR voltage drop is reduced, and thinner and smaller Micro-OLED wafer-level packaging with better electrical performance is realized.

sources.title: Micro OLED device structure and display equipment [CN224250121U]
sources.abstract: The utility model provides a Micro OLED device structure and a display device, and relates to the technical field of OLEDs. The organic light emitting layer is arranged on the anode; the cathode is arranged on the organic light emitting layer; and the light filtering lens layer is arranged on the cathode, and the light filtering lens layer comprises a plurality of quantum dot light filtering lenses. The filter lens layer is arranged to replace a traditional color filter layer and a lens, so that the problem of overall brightness loss caused by the color filter and the lens is solved.

draft.summary: OLED displays are a commercially established technology: filings describe a growing share of the display market and a value chain of IP licensing, glass, driver chips and microdisplays (M1, M2, M3, M6, M8). Research activity is rising (18.5% YoY in 2025 and 66.7% year-to-date in 2026), though some of the paper count is OLED used only as a component in unrelated devices (S12). Patent filing is roughly flat (P1-P4 and code counts). The main open issues are blue-emitter stability, burn-in, large-area manufacturing cost and competition from LCD and micro-LED (R1-R4, C2). Social signals are mixed: Counterpoint expects smartphone OLED shipments to fall about 3% in 2026, while Apple, Motorola and laptop makers are reported to be adding OLED (X1-X3, X6). Related stocks are mixed, with two in sharp drawdowns and Universal Display near its recent high (T7). Several science findings were weakened by Risk challenges (C1-C7), and there is no direct evidence on order volumes, margins or market share.
draft.plain_summary: OLED screens are the bright, thin displays already used in many premium phones, TVs and laptops, and they are slowly spreading into cars and VR headsets. Research and company activity suggest the technology is established rather than speculative. The main thing that could hold it back is that the blue light-emitting material still wears out faster than the others, which causes screen burn-in and raises costs against cheaper LCD screens.

horizons.assessment: Filings show OLED already sold across many device types and licensed to a major panel maker (M1, M2). Social signals point to continued product launches in premium phones and laptops (X2, X6), but Counterpoint expects OLED smartphone panel shipments to fall about 3% in 2026 on memory-supply and cost pressure (X1). Universal Display is up 20.1% in a month while Corning and Kopin are in drawdowns (T3, T5, T1), so near-term timing risk is mixed.

horizons.label: forecast

These are mostly social-media claims and early signals. LCD with full-array local dimming has a cost and supply-chain advantage in automotive (R4).

horizons.label: forecast
horizons.assessment: The evidence says little directly about 3-5 years. The case depends on OLED keeping its share against LCD and micro-LED (R4) and on manufacturing cost falling (R3). Ostin Technology notes that industry-wide capacity expansion is a risk and that OLED may gain wider acceptance (M7). That is a company statement, not a market forecast.

base.label: forecast

bear.label: forecast
